Exercise: Smith Machine One-Arm Upright Row

Category:
strength

Exercise Type:
compound

Force Type:
pull

Difficulty Level:
beginner

Movement Patterns:

- external_rotation
- unilateral_shoulder_abduction

Primary Muscles:

- shoulders

Secondary Muscles:

- biceps
- traps

Equipment:

- machine

Fatigue Score:
3

Systemic Fatigue:
low

Stimulus To Fatigue Ratio:
2.5

Energy Requirement:
moderate

Recovery Time:
1 hours

Goals:

- build_upper_body_muscle_mass
- develop_shoulder_strength_and_stability

Contraindications:

- Shoulder instability or injury
- Rotator cuff issues

Exercise Variations:

- name: Kettlebell One-Arm Upright Row, equipment: kettlebell
- name: Barbell Upright Row, equipment: barbell

Substitution Options:

- name: Dumbbell One-Arm Upright Row, equipment: free weights

Instructions:

- With the bar at thigh level, load an appropriate weight.
- Take a wide grip on the bar and unhook the weight, removing your off hand from the bar. Your arm should be extended as you stand up straight with your head and chest up. This will be your starting position.
- Begin the movement by flexing the elbow, raising the upper arm with the elbow pointed out. Continue until your upper arm is parallel to the floor.
- After a brief pause, return the weight to the starting position.
- Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before engaging the hooks to rack the weight.
